sn36.23:1.1: Then a certain bhikkhu approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, sat down to one side, and said to him:
sn36.23:1.2: “Venerable sir, what now is feeling? What is the origin of feeling? What is the way leading to the origination of feeling?
sn36.23:1.3: What is the cessation of feeling? What is the way leading to the cessation of feeling?
sn36.23:1.4: What is the gratification in feeling? What is the danger? What is the escape?”
sn36.23:2.2: pleasant feeling, painful feeling, neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling.
sn36.23:2.4: With the arising of contact there is the arising of feeling.
sn36.23:2.5: Craving is the way leading to the origination of feeling.
sn36.23:2.6: With the cessation of contact there is the cessation of feeling.
sn36.23:2.7: This Noble Eightfold Path is the way leading to the cessation of feeling; that is,
sn36.23:2.9: “The pleasure and joy that arise in dependence on feeling: this is the gratification in feeling.
sn36.23:2.10: That feeling is impermanent, suffering, and subject to change: this is the danger in feeling.
sn36.23:2.11: The removal and abandonment of desire and lust for feeling: this is the escape from feeling.”
